title: Strict henselization preserves embedding dimension
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local commutative ring and let $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ be its strict henselization with respect to a separable closure $\kappa^{\mathrm{sep}}$ of $\kappa$. Write $\mathfrak m^{\mathrm{sh}}$ for the maximal ideal of $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$. Then the canonical base-change map $(\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2)\otimes_{\kappa}\kappa^{\mathrm{sep}}\to\mathfrak m^{\mathrm{sh}}/(\mathfrak m^{\mathrm{sh}})^2$ is an isomorphism of $\kappa^{\mathrm{sep}}$-vector spaces. In particular, $\dim_{\kappa}(\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2)=\dim_{\kappa^{\mathrm{sep}}}(\mathfrak m^{\mathrm{sh}}/(\mathfrak m^{\mathrm{sh}})^2)$.

proof.text: Apply Algebra.strictHenselization_local_maximalIdeal to the given pointed-algebra strict henselization. It supplies an IsLocalRing instance on C and maximalIdeal C = (maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R C). Use IsStrictHenselization.triples_presentation to present this same C as a universal cocone of the residue-triple diagram, with the original structural map. Apply strictHenselization_faithfullyFlat to that cocone and convert its ring-hom faithful flatness into Module.FaithfullyFlat R C; in particular C is flat over R.

proof.text: Specialize Mathlib Ideal.tensorCotangentHom_injective_of_flat and Ideal.tensorCotangentHom_surjective to the base algebra R itself and the flat algebra C. They give bijectivity of C tensor_R I.Cotangent to the cotangent module of I extended to C tensor_R R. Transport the extended ideal and its cotangent module along Algebra.TensorProduct.rid R C C. The induced map on cotangent modules is bijective because the map induced by the inverse algebra equivalence is a two-sided inverse; check both compositions on the surjective maps Ideal.toCotangent. On pure tensors of cotangent classes, the composite is exactly LinearMap.liftBaseChange C (Ideal.mapCotangent I J (Algebra.ofId R C) h). Set I = maximalIdeal R and J = maximalIdeal C, using the equality from Step 1. This proves the exact canonical-map bijectivity in the statement.

The maximal-ideal containment makes algebraMap R C a local homomorphism, so Mathlib supplies the canonical residue-field algebra structure. Turn the bijective C-linear map of Step 2 into a linear equivalence and base change it to the residue field l of C. The tensor associativity/cancellation equivalence identifies its source with l tensor_R CotangentSpace R. Surjectivity of R to its residue field k gives compatible scalar actions, hence a canonical l-linear equivalence from l tensor_k CotangentSpace R to l tensor_R CotangentSpace R. Similarly surjectivity of C to l identifies l tensor_C CotangentSpace C with CotangentSpace C. Compose these equivalences. Module.finrank_baseChange and LinearEquiv.finrank_eq give the asserted equality. No finite-dimensionality assumption is necessary for this finrank comparison.
